one_month_reasoning: Events in the window: ASML Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-14 (guide EUR 11.0-12.0B, GM 55-57%; consensus Q3 EPS ~EUR 10.65), TSMC Q3 results and capex commentary on 2026-10-15, then Lam and KLA results in late October. Industry data into the print is strong. Micron (2026-09-30) said memory supply will be 'much tighter' in FY27-28 with no line of sight to balance, and that 2027 HBM is mostly sold at higher prices. TrendForce sees 4Q26 DRAM contract prices up 10-20%. Brokers have TSMC 2027 capex at $77-85B, and management says 2027 is close to fully booked. I expect a beat and constructive 2027 commentary, but ASML does not publish quarterly bookings any more, so the print offers less of an upside surprise lever. And the stock has already bounced about 15% from ~$1,575 on 2026-09-15 to $1,808 on the Micron-led equipment rally, so part of the good news is in the price. The MATCH Act risk inside the window is low: the FY27 NDAA is stalled in the Senate and has not gone to conference, and chip controls were not discussed at the 2026-09-24 Trump-Xi summit. Net: no strong directional edge after the rebound. I used a lognormal with median ~$1,815 at ~13.5% monthly vol (46%/3.5, nudged up for the earnings print).

fair_value.method: 60% forward P/E (2028E EPS ~EUR 59.5 = ~$67 x 29x = ~$1,943) and 40% FCF yield (2028E FCF/share ~EUR 56 = ~$63 at a 3.25% yield = ~$1,940), blended to ~$1,940 for the stock 12 months out.

inputs_detail.derivation: ASML's +30% capacity plan, cross-checked against Zeiss SMT's +20-25% EUV optics capacity for 2027 (Kuo: 80-85 EUV, 380-400 DUV)

The implied Q4 2026 run rate (~EUR 14.4B = 44B guide midpoint less H1 and Q3 guide) annualizes to ~EUR 57B. Consensus is EUR 54.6B (range 43.6-60.7). Customer capex is rising: TSMC 2027 capex at $77-85B per brokers, Micron FY27 capex higher, Samsung P5 (~20 EUV) and SK hynix (~20 EUV through 2027). Lam sees 8-10 new tier-1 fabs through 2027. I sit slightly above consensus.

EUR 56.5B x ~57% GM = 32.2B; less R&D/SG&A ~6.9B = EBIT ~25.3B; ~17% tax = ~21.0B; / ~380M shares = ~EUR 55, trimmed to 54 for opex and mix risk. Consensus is EUR 51.73 (33 analysts, range 37.4-59.1; Yahoo shows EUR). This corrects my round-1 file, which treated the 51.72 consensus as USD.

~10% growth over 2027. Positives: like-for-like EUV price rises that can only land on 2028+ shipments because backlog prices are fixed (RBC, Tom's Hardware), memory High-NA from 2028, ASML studying another +30% capacity, and Micron seeing tight supply through 2028. Haircut because consensus hyperscaler capex growth slows sharply into 2028 (Goldman: 54% in 2027 to ~12% in 2028).

Today: $1,808 / (EUR 51.73 x 1.125 = $58.2) = ~31x 2027 consensus and ~30x my NTM. 24/7 Wall St put it at 28x forward at $1,575. I assume a mild de-rating toward ~29x as the market looks at 2028 growth that is decelerating (the usual late-cycle equipment pattern).

inputs_detail.derivation: ~EUR 22.6B net income (2028E EPS x shares), ~93% cash conversion after capex for the new Eindhoven campus (ground broken September 2026) and capacity expansion, partly offset by customer down-payments in a sold-out market
Basic weighted shares went from 385.4M (Q1 2026) to ~382M (Q2: EUR 2.9B / EPS 7.59). Ongoing buybacks (EUR 1.1B in Q2) retire ~1% a year.
A 29x P/E is a 3.45% earnings yield; times ~0.93 FCF conversion gives ~3.2%

bear.story: In 2027 markets start to treat the cycle as peaking. Hyperscaler capex growth decelerates toward ~12% for 2028, memory prices roll over once Micron, SK hynix and Samsung fabs (ID1, M15X, Yongin, P5) ramp in 2027-28, and 2028 EUV orders disappoint. The MATCH Act rides a revived NDAA and bans DUV sales and servicing for named Chinese fabs (China was ~20% of 2026 sales). 2028 EPS gets cut to ~$55 and the multiple falls to ~22x.

base.story: 2027 sales ~EUR 56B on 80-85 EUV units with GM ~57%. The 2028 outlook is for further growth on EUV pricing and memory High-NA. EPS ~$61 (2027) / ~$67 (2028) at ~29-30x forward.

bull.story: ASML confirms another +30% capacity step for 2028, like-for-like EUV price increases stick, TSMC 2027 capex comes in at $85B+ and memory makers pull High-NA orders forward. MATCH stays stalled. 2028 EPS ~$75 at ~37x.

thesis_break_reason: About 20.5x my 2027E EPS (~$61) and ~31% below today. A sustained trade there would most likely mean the 2027-28 growth case broke (EUV slots pushed out, a memory capex cut as prices roll over, or a China DUV sales and servicing ban enacted), not ordinary 46%-vol noise. The stock already hit ~$1,575 in mid-September on worry alone, so a $1,250 level needs fundamental damage.

reasoning: Continuation round with the search budget restored (~27 more searches/fetches). Industry-lane evidence for 2027 got stronger. Micron (2026-09-30) sees supply 'much tighter' in FY27-28 and is lifting capex. TrendForce has 4Q26 DRAM contract prices up 10-20%. Brokers put TSMC 2027 capex at $77-85B, against $60-64B in 2026. Lam sees 8-10 new tier-1 fabs through 2027. Zeiss is adding 20-25% EUV optics capacity, consistent with 80-85 EUV units in 2027. RBC and Tom's Hardware point to like-for-like EUV price rises landing on 2028+ shipments. A key correction: the 2027 EPS consensus of 51.73 is in EUR, not USD (Yahoo; the Q3 EPS consensus of 10.65 reconciles with the EUR guide). So the stock trades at ~31x 2027, not 35x, and my 2027 EPS rises to ~EUR 54. The bear case also has new weight. Consensus hyperscaler capex growth decelerates sharply into 2028, which matches the late-cycle de-rating base rate. Large memory fab ramps in 2027-28 could turn memory prices. The stock already fell to ~$1,575 in mid-September on valuation and China worries before rebounding ~15%. MATCH Act risk is lower near-term but not gone: the NDAA is stalled over the Iran war, the Trump-Xi summit skipped chip controls, and China's domestic lithography (SMEE 28nm DUV in validation, EUV ~2028-30) is a long-dated threat. Fair value rises from $1,880 to ~$1,940 and the scenario mean is ~$2,025. For the ladder I used a lognormal with median ~$1,930, sigma 0.42 above the median and 0.47 below (a fatter left tail for cycle and policy shocks), below the 46% realized vol, which the 2025-26 re-rating inflated. Limits: Twelve Data / Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints were unavailable (plan/rate limit); X was not used; I found no liquid prediction market on the MATCH Act or the FY27 NDAA.
